rv.q: Their heartfelt performances serve as a powerful reminder that grief is myriad, and that in the end, it is the human connection through empathy that saves us all.
Specific details like that, ultimately, make this evening incredibly worthwhile.
McKenzie-Voigt and Nally have wonderful chemistry onstage, both while playing piano and singing, and in their moments of high emotion and quiet humanity.
The show's core conversation is hugely resonant, and I was grateful to watch it play out the way it did.

cn.t: Critics praise this intimate two-hander for its emotional depth and poignant exploration of identity and grief, though the central reveal proves unsurprising. The 25-seat setting enhances the personal connection between teacher and student.
